lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing, Python
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Check that the profile link is live and complete.
Consider adding relevant MBA coursework or activities if they earn their space.
items.because: You are applying to product roles.

items.says: Clarify whether the under-five-day dry-dock figure is an average, a consistently met target, or an improvement.
Add scale or an outcome for the hydraulic systems and records work.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities rather than accomplishments.

items.says: Be ready to explain the move from the MBA and product internship to the full-time mechanic role.
items.because: An unexplained pivot may distract readers considering you for product roles.

items.says: Specify whether the 2,300 merchants were in the measured cohort.
Check that the timing and before-and-after comparison support the claimed reduction.
Distinguish the five-percentage-point conversion increase from a 5% increase.
Verify the flow was shipped to all merchants rather than merely approved.
items.because: The rollout claim should appear only if it was shipped.

items.says: Explain the RICE Reach scoring basis accurately or remove the methodology detail.
items.because: Tickets a feature would close are not necessarily the users or events it would reach.

items.says: State the chargeback roadmap decision or outcome more specifically.
items.because: “Set the priority” does not show what changed.

items.says: Clarify the unit of analysis and avoid implying a customer-level effect without supporting analysis.
items.because: The A/B test was randomized by session.

items.says: The checkout lift repeats a result in the earlier checkout bullet.
items.because: The bullets overlap unless the methods detail adds distinct evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether rollout funding was approved, allocated, or spent.
Show how the scorecards informed contract or carrier changes.
items.because: Otherwise the drop in late deliveries reads as more directly caused by the scorecards than the bullet establishes.

items.says: Clarify your ownership versus the supervisors’ role.
Specify whether the 30% reduction is relative.
Define the forecast-error measure.
items.because: Readers could interpret the 18% and 11% figures in different ways.

items.says: Separate or trim the activities in the route-planning bullet.
items.because: It covers too much for your contribution to the 1,800-hour saving to be easy to follow.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 means registered users, active users, or students with access.
Confirm that the nine-tonne figure was measured.
Define the period meant by “first year.”
The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Distinguish whether interviews led you to choose reminders or established that reminders caused the growth.
The rise from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
Substantiate the attribution of the fill-rate increase to the volunteer system.
Verify that the food-rescue project’s “Present” date is accurate alongside the full-time role.
Make clear that $2.4M is estimated annual savings, not realized savings.
Clarify what you personally did on patient intake.
items.because: The passive construction obscures your contribution.

items.says: Clarify what changed after front-desk staff adopted the intake changes.
The pilot approval repeats the preceding pilot-funding outcome.
items.because: The bullets substantially overlap unless each adds distinct evidence.

items.says: Consider separating Python from product practices.
Give the product internship and project the most space if targeting product roles.
items.because: Operations and mechanic experience should not crowd out the clearest product evidence.
